name: Hamor
overview: Hamor was a male member of the Hivite tribe, known specifically as the father of Shechem. His identity is primarily marked by his tribal affiliation and paternal role within the biblical narrative, with no additional personal notes recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Hamor is a proper name meaning "donkey" in Hebrew. This name is not indicated as being given by God, but it identifies him distinctly in the scriptural account.
familyAndRelationships: Hamor is explicitly identified as the father of Shechem and a descendant of Hivi, establishing his place within the Hivite lineage. He is also connected indirectly to Simeon and Levi, who are noted as victims in the same narrative context.
scriptureSignificance: Hamor's significance in Scripture arises from his role as the father of Shechem, placing him at a pivotal point in the interactions between the Hivites and the descendants of Jacob. His family ties and tribal identity contribute to the unfolding events involving Simeon and Levi, highlighting the broader relational dynamics among the tribes during this period.
